answer: Stop sybils with a violet dye, a vine, and a gale. Each identity's bond is dipped in violet dye, a stain that travels along the vine of endorsements linking it to its sponsors, so every clone funded from one purse carries the same violet mark. The k-th identity sharing one dye batch posts k squared in bond, so N clones pay roughly N cubed for one shared stain. Once per epoch a gale blows through the registry and strips a random sample; any identity whose violet matches a stripped neighbour loses its bond. One honest agent risks one dyed bond; a clone factory pays N cubed to hide one stain.
